name: MedWeb checklist
description: Background Social media offers valuable information for public health surveillance, but detecting valid symptom expressions in noisy and informal text remains challenging. Fine-tuned language models can achieve strong test accuracy while relying on spurious patterns, limiting their reliability in real-world applications. Objective This study aimed to develop a more robust symptom detection model by incorporating surveillance-relevant attributes into the training objective and introducing a counterfactual-based evaluation framework to assess attribute sensitivity. Methods We proposed a concept-aware learning framework (CALF), which combines multiattribute counterfactual data augmentation with multitask learning. We compared standard fine-tuning (baseline) with data-level interventions, a model-level intervention, hybrid strategies, and prompt-based methods across multiple encoders and LLMs for data augmentation. Performance was evaluated on the following 3 datasets: the MedWeb test using macro F1-score (m-F1), the MedWeb checklist using flip accuracy (FA), and a supplementary test set using F1-score for flu-or-fever detection (f-F1). FA measures sensitivity to surveillance-relevant attributes, and the supplementary test score serves as an indicator for out-of-distribution performance. Results The baseline achieved an m-F1-score of 0.871 on the test set but a low overall FA on the checklist (FA=0.342).
